verdict_basis: Zero blocking findings. The contract's load-bearing laws were verified mechanically against the committed bytes: the seam is consulted only at the two Add* preparation sites and never through cache_options (full-tree census); BF-1's two-hash split is real and the observed _stage_key stays role-free so engine result-key composition is unchanged; the extracted derivations are byte-verbatim (ast-slice normalized diff vs f139dd3: 48/48 network lines identical, snap identical except the moved store block); public artifacts are bitwise equal with the route armed (island E1 test plus this review's independent 3-row serial-vs-W2 sha256 tree re-run: 6 artifacts, trees equal); read/validation/failure chronology is preserved (snapshot read + digest strictly before the flight consult at both seams; file-disappearance and same-size-mtime invalidation tests green); the detach law holds on the success path (delta taken then una and topology detached before capture/state-bundle) AND on the exception path (empirical: a mid-row FileNotFoundError with the session attached yields a failed RowResult that pickles cleanly at 633 bytes with no state_bundle and empty settings_post); the empty-payload owner law works (probe: fresh root, owner ({}, None) commits 0 entries and never poisons the next build); the registry is bounded at 4 with oldest eviction (probe: 6 touched roots -> 4 retained, close/reopen correct); refusal taxonomy falls back to the byte-identical original path because prep=None joins the unmodified cache-off body. The seven non-blocking findings below are diagnostic-surface fidelity, counters/reporting gaps, evidence-coverage and claim-precision items, each with a bounded repair.

non_blocking.what_is_wrong: The prepared AddNetwork branch returns at line 282 before the unconditional tail line 321, so the OWNER (cold-build) row's log stream misses the v=2 line ('create topology', "edge_list_dict created") that the current path always emits. The pre-P02I body logged it unconditionally at AddNetwork's end (f139dd3 old line 323).
non_blocking.failure_scenario: Any parallel accessibility run with the route armed: the owner rows' row-log streams differ from the serial/current route by one missing v=2 line. Artifacts are unaffected (verified bitwise), so no comparator breaks; the divergence is on a diagnostic surface and is invisible to E2, whose filter only compares event=='Network added' entries.
non_blocking.verified_by: Probe A (_p02r_probes.py): original vs prepared-owner event dumps on the smoke fixture - owner stream lacks exactly that line; all other lines byte-identical.
non_blocking.minimal_repair: Log ('create topology', "edge_list_dict created", v=2) in the prepared owner/fallback branch before the return (or move the tail line above the early return so both paths share it). 2-line diff + a stream-parity assertion.

non_blocking.what_is_wrong: The prepared HIT stream misses the v=2 line ('create topology', "edge_sindex created") that the produce path emits inside Network.BuildTopology. The audit's section-10 replay inventory (the amended contract text the restore follows) itself omits this line, so the restore satisfies the inventory but not the actual uncached v<=2 stream. Consequence: owner and hit 'create topology' streams differ from each other (owner: edge_sindex created only; hit: edge_list_dict created only), and each differs from the current path. The E2 gate compares only the 'Network added' event subset, so it establishes less than the claimed 'log-stream parity modulo the hit's own announcement'.
non_blocking.failure_scenario: Parallel run with the route armed: every hit row's stream misses one content-derived v=2 line relative to the current route. No artifact, chronology, or result impact (probe C trees bitwise-equal); NF-1's 'CRS set to EPSG:3857.' line IS replayed correctly (probe A confirms the crs_label mechanism works).
non_blocking.verified_by: Probe A event dumps (original / prepared owner / prepared hit); audit section 10 text re-read; E2 test source inspected (filter is event=='Network added' only).
non_blocking.minimal_repair: Replay ('create topology', "edge_sindex created", v=2) in _restore_network_from_cache and add it to audit section 10's inventory; or record it explicitly as an accepted divergence the way CACHE_GRAPH's missing CRS line was recorded. Amend the E2 test to compare full streams modulo the announcement.

non_blocking.what_is_wrong: (a) The contract counters_law names corruption_rebuild as a distinct counter; it exists nowhere - the module docstring says 'store stats at report time' but no code reads store stats into the report; a corrupt-entry rebuild is only visible as cold_build. (b) distinct identities are not in the report, so the NF-7 gate (builds <= distinct identities, equality only when contention-fallback counters are zero) is checkable only inside tests; for a stage whose payload is unrepresentable (reachable in the admitted domain: a mixed-dimension geojson layer yields payload None -> the ({}, None) sentinel) every row becomes owner and builds with fallback_compute==0, which violates the letter of NF-7 while being behaviorally correct (each row computes locally exactly as the current path).
non_blocking.failure_scenario: A post-hoc auditor reading extra['preparation'] cannot evaluate the NF-7 engagement law or detect corruption-rebuild activity from public evidence; a mixed-dim input run would report cold_build==rows==identities-looking numbers that no reported quantity can contradict.
non_blocking.verified_by: Code read of the aggregation block and PrepSession.counters; grep confirms no store.stats() consumer in the batch layer; probe 2 confirms the empty/unrepresentable owner path leaves 0 entries and counts cold_build per row.
non_blocking.minimal_repair: Aggregate store.stats() (hits/misses/quarantined) and a distinct-identity count into extra['preparation'] at report time (the session/flight already sees every key), and record the NF-7 boundary for unrepresentable stages in the contract amendments.

non_blocking.what_is_wrong: The EMPTY-PAYLOAD law - the commit's 'defect 3', the one law whose violation would poison every waiter - has no committed regression test. The island's ({}, None) producers (test_served_copy_mutation_isolation, lines 218/221) only ever execute on HIT paths where the owner branch is never reached; prepared_L0_L2.json attributes the law's evidence to the uncommitted _p02i_smoke.py area 8.
non_blocking.failure_scenario: A future refactor of Flight.arrays_once that drops the 'if arrays:' guard would pass the entire committed suite while re-introducing the poisoned-empty-entry defect.
non_blocking.verified_by: This review verified the law works today (probe 2: fresh root, owner ({}, None) -> StageProduced, store entries 0, nothing retained; subsequent real producer builds and commits normally), which is exactly the test that is missing from the island.
non_blocking.minimal_repair: Add the probe as a committed test: fresh root, owner returning ({}, None), assert 0 store entries + StageProduced, then a real producer on the same key builds/serves correct bits.

non_blocking.what_is_wrong: Flight's owner-branch commit guard is weaker than the StageCache.put_arrays machinery it mirrors: it guards on `if arrays:` (truthy dict) and catches TypeError only. A producer returning a non-empty dict whose encode drops every entry (e.g. {'x': None}) raises ValueError ('payload must contain at least one named blob') out of arrays_once, failing the row loudly instead of leaving the stage uncached. Unreachable from the two v1 producers (both payload builders return the ({}, None) sentinel whenever geometry_wkb is absent), so this is a latent robustness gap, not a live bug.
non_blocking.failure_scenario: Increment A widens the producer set (feather/parquet fixtures, new stages): a producer that can return all-None arrays would turn 'stage stays uncached' into a hard row failure - a contract fallback-law violation of the silent kind the flight is supposed to prevent.
non_blocking.verified_by: Probe 2: all-None producer raises ValueError through arrays_once; store.py:194-217 put() rejects empty payload mappings; cache/stages.py:132-152 put_arrays() refuses empty encodes and catches TypeError.
non_blocking.minimal_repair: Compute payload = encode_arrays(arrays) once, commit only `if payload:`, keeping the TypeError catch - identical shape to StageCache.put_arrays. 3-line diff.

non_blocking.what_is_wrong: The commit message claims 'serial and single-job runs never arm the prepared route', but the negative test covers only serial RunBatch and a direct RunAccessibility call. A single-row PARALLEL RunBatch arms the route: runtime.py gates on analysis=='accessibility' and dispatchable being non-empty, with no row-count condition.

non_blocking.verified_by: Probe B output (root exists, extra keys [cohort, preparation], counters rows=1/stages=3/cold_build=3); runtime.py:970-1000 arming conditions; test_serial_and_single_job_never_arm_the_prepared_route read.
